32-1.title: Check that the foreign school or programme is recognised before you pay tuition
32-1.inPlainWords: India has no single 'approved school' list for every country. Check the institution's recognition with its national regulator, the Indian embassy or consulate, and the UGC or the AIU if you want the degree recognised in India. A scholarship or a visa may depend on the institution's recognition. Do not pay an agent for a 'guaranteed' admission or a 'recognised' degree.
32-1.benefit: The UGC and the Association of Indian Universities publish the recognition and equivalence rules for a foreign degree. The destination's education ministry or regulator lists the accredited institutions. The Indian mission can confirm whether a college is genuine. A student visa usually requires an admission letter from a recognised institution. A fake university can leave you with a degree that no employer or university accepts.
32-1.cost: No cost to check the regulator's list. A credential evaluation may have a fee.
32-1.caveats: A 'pathway' college that is not accredited may not lead to a degree. Check the course, the campus and the recognition separately. Do not pay the full tuition before the admission letter is verified.
32-1.sources: University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>; Association of Indian Universities. <https://www.aiu.ac.in/>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>

32-9.title: Allow time for degree equivalence and document attestation before you return to India
32-9.inPlainWords: A foreign degree may need an equivalence certificate from the Association of Indian Universities for a government job or a higher degree, and the documents may need an apostille or a consular attestation. Start before you leave: collect the transcript, the degree certificate and the marksheets, and check the AIU's current rules. A private agent cannot make an unrecognised degree recognised.
32-9.benefit: The Association of Indian Universities issues an equivalence certificate for a foreign degree, and the Ministry of External Affairs attests documents for use abroad or in India. The Hague Apostille Convention applies to some countries. A government employer or a university may ask for the equivalence and the attestation. The process takes weeks, so plan ahead.
32-9.cost: The AIU fee is modest; an agent's fee is avoidable. Attestation has a fee.
32-9.caveats: A degree from an unrecognised institution may not get equivalence. Check the AIU list and the course duration. Keep the original documents; a photocopy is not enough.
32-9.sources: Association of Indian Universities. <https://www.aiu.ac.in/>; Ministry of External Affairs, attestation. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>

32-2.title: A U.S. court has put the fixed-stay rule for F-1 students on hold: 'duration of status' still applies for now
32-2.inPlainWords: The U.S. proposed to replace 'stay until you finish your course' with a fixed maximum stay of four years and a 30-day window to leave afterwards. A federal court stayed the rule one day before it was to take effect, so the older rules still apply while the case continues: you may stay for the length of your programme, and you get 60 days after you finish to leave or change status. A stay is not a repeal. The government can appeal, and the rule could come back in amended form. Write the programme end date on your I-20 into your calendar, and check your university's international student office page each term.
32-2.benefit: The rule was announced in July 2026 with an effective date of 15 September 2026. It would have ended 'duration of status' for F, J and I visa holders and substituted a fixed four-year admission with an extension application. On 14 September 2026 a U.S. District Court in Massachusetts stayed it nationwide under section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act; the court did not vacate the rule, and the government can appeal. While the stay stands, F-1 students keep the current position: admission for the duration of status, and a 60-day grace period after the programme ends.
32-2.cost: No cost. Note the programme end date from your I-20 and set a reminder about 90 days ahead. The I-20 is the form your school issues to certify your eligibility for F-1 status. Check the international student office page once a semester rather than relying on social media.
32-2.caveats: This is a court stay, not a final decision, and the position can change at short notice. If the rule is revived, an extension would have to be filed before your authorised stay expires; there is no automatic renewal. The proposal also covered J visas, with different details, so check the rule for your own visa category. Students planning a multi-year programme, a transfer or a post-study work period should not assume the current position will last. Ask the international student office before you travel or change course.
32-2.sources: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, No. 1:26-cv-13799-FDS (order of 14 September 2026). <https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74661796/presidents-alliance-on-higher-education-and-immigration-v-united-states/>; 8 CFR 214.2(f), students and exchange visitors. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. <https://www.uscis.gov/>

32-6.title: Read the MEA's travel advisory for your destination and the Indian mission's student notices before you go
32-6.inPlainWords: India does not publish a country-by-country list of 'unsafe' study destinations. What the government does publish is the Ministry of External Affairs' travel advisories, and each Indian embassy or consulate posts local security, visa and consular notices, often including ones for students. Read the advisory for your destination before you pay a deposit, and check the mission's page once a term. An advisory is the government's written assessment of conditions there: if it says to avoid non-essential travel, treat that as a real signal rather than as paperwork.
32-6.benefit: The Ministry of External Affairs lists current travel advisories by country, and the list of Indian missions and posts links to the embassy or consulate that covers your city. A mission's page carries local notices, consular contact details and, in a crisis, instructions for Indian nationals. Together with the destination government's own travel advice and your institution's international office, these are the written sources you can point to when a family member or an employer asks whether a place is safe. A mission can also tell you which local lawyer or doctor to approach after an accident or a crime.
32-6.cost: Free. Read it once before you commit to a course and once each semester; a two-minute check is cheaper than a ruined year.
32-6.caveats: Advisories change without notice and this page cannot stay current, so read the MEA page itself. An advisory is not a ban: it does not decide your visa, and a university may still admit you. It can matter for insurance and for a scholarship, so keep a printout with your documents. The mission cannot get your agent's fee back or overrule a foreign court. Save the mission's address and emergency number in your phone before you fly.
32-6.sources: Ministry of External Affairs, travel advisories. <https://www.mea.gov.in/travel-advisories.htm>; Ministry of External Affairs, Indian missions and posts abroad. <https://www.mea.gov.in/indian-mission-abroad.htm>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>

32-10.title: Before you enrol, check how the degree will be recognised in India: AIU equivalence, MEA attestation and the professional council
32-10.inPlainWords: There is no Indian list that flags particular foreign universities. What decides your future is whether the degree will be accepted here: the Association of Indian Universities issues an equivalence certificate for a foreign degree, the Ministry of External Affairs apostilles or attests your documents, and for a professional course the relevant council decides recognition. A programme sold as 'no language test, no need to travel, master's in a few months' is exactly the kind that fails that check. Verify before you pay, not after.
32-10.benefit: AIU equivalence is what a government employer, a public university or a higher degree usually asks for. MEA attestation or an apostille is what makes an Indian document usable abroad, and a foreign document usable here. For a professional course the council that regulates the profession also has a say: the National Medical Commission for medicine, the dental council for dentistry, the Bar Council of India for law, and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India for accountancy. The UGC's rules on foreign degrees and on online and distance programmes decide whether a course delivered mostly online counts at all. None of these steps can be skipped by an agent.
32-10.cost: AIU equivalence and MEA attestation both charge a fee, and both take weeks rather than days. An agent's 'guaranteed equivalence' or 'fast-track certification' fee buys nothing that you cannot do yourself.
32-10.caveats: Equivalence is decided case by case, on the syllabus, the duration, the mode of study and the institution's recognition in its own country, so a name that sounds familiar is not enough. A professional council's recognition is a separate question from AIU equivalence: clearing one does not give you the other. A degree awarded for a course delivered online, or by an institution that is not recognised where it operates, may get no equivalence at all, and no payment can change that. Anyone offering to certify a degree through an 'internal channel' is running a fraud.
32-10.sources: Association of Indian Universities, equivalence of degrees. <https://aiu.ac.in/frontpage/equivalence-of-degree/>; Association of Indian Universities, equivalence committee. <https://aiu.ac.in/governance/equivalence-commitee/>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>; National Medical Commission. <https://www.nmc.org.in/>; Bar Council of India. <https://www.bci.org.in/>; Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. <https://www.icai.org/>

32-3.title: The maximum allowed work hours are strict limits in the U.S., Canada, UK, and Australia — exceeding them violates visa terms.
32-3.cost: There’s no cost involved. You simply need to track your weekly hours yourself. The difficulty lies in employers often claiming “no one checks extra hours,” but you must never believe this.
32-3.inPlainWords: All four countries set clear caps on how many hours international students may work. Going over these limits breaches visa conditions, potentially leading to visa revocation, deportation, or extra scrutiny during future applications. The limits are: 20 hours per week in the U.S., 20 hours weekly for degree students and 10 hours for non-degree students in the UK, 24 hours per week in Canada, and 48 hours every two weeks in Australia. Hours worked at multiple jobs must be combined.
32-3.benefit: F-1 students in the U.S. may work up to 20 hours per week on campus during term time, with the same 20-hour weekly cap applying to approved off-campus jobs; full-time work is allowed during holidays. This is stipulated under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9) of U.S. federal immigration regulations. UK students pursuing degree-level courses may work 20 hours weekly during term time, while those on non-degree programs are limited to 10 hours per week; no work is permitted for part-time students at all. Self-employment is also prohibited, meaning you cannot work for yourself, nor may you serve as a professional athlete or performer. These rules are outlined in the UK immigration rules for students, specifically Student ST26.1 and ST26.5. Eligible full-time students in Canada may work up to 24 hours per week off campus, per paragraph 186(v) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). For Australian student visas, the limit is 48 hours every two weeks while classes are in session; this restriction does not apply to research-based master’s or PhD students, nor their dependents.
32-3.sources: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student (ST26.1, ST26.5). <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student>; IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html>; Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500>
32-3.caveats: In the U.S., any off-campus work must first receive official approval; you cannot begin working while your I-765 work permit application is still pending. Older Canadian work permits may list a 20-hour weekly cap, but if you still meet all eligibility criteria, current regulations permit up to 24 hours per week. The UK’s self-employment ban is broadly interpreted: taking private contracts, running an online store, or working as a freelancer all count as prohibited self-employment.
